source_text: concupiscentiam non usquequaque animo rebellem: procul dubio confiteris rebellem: et supplicium non fateris, quo adversus te ipsum bellum geris? Dicatur parvulorum creator Deus talium, quales Dei manibus digni sunt"; et addis, "id est, innocentium
pass_a_gloss: Desire not usquequaque to-the-soul rebellem: far dubio confiteris rebellem: and punishment not fateris, whither adversus you itself war geris? Dicatur parvulorum creator God such, quales of-God manibus digni are "; and addis, " it is, innocentium.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Sexual desire is not wholly rebellious against the mind.
Let God be called the creator of infants who are such as befit God’s hands—that is, innocent infants.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
